name: localpilot-agent
description: The AI coding agent that runs on your machine. Copilot-style agent mode with Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM — private, offline, free.

localpilot.providers.markdownDescription: Local and cloud model servers. `type` is `ollama` (native API, local or Ollama Cloud), `openai` (any OpenAI-compatible API: LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang, LocalAI, Jan, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Azure OpenAI…), `anthropic` (Claude) or `vscode-lm` (models VS Code offers through its Language Model API, such as GitHub Copilot; VS Code only, no `baseUrl` needed). Models are referenced as `<id>/<model>`. Automatic model picks prefer local models; cloud models are used when you choose them or nothing local fits.

id.description: Short unique id, e.g. ollama, lmstudio

apiKey.markdownDescription: API key. Keep it out of this file with `${env:OPENAI_API_KEY}` (an environment variable) or **LocalPilot: Set Provider API Key…**, which stores it in VS Code secret storage and writes `${secret:<id>}` here.

cloud.markdownDescription: The server sends prompts to cloud models although it runs locally (gateways such as OmniRoute or LiteLLM). Automatic model picks then prefer local models over it. Unset: decided by the URL.

models.description: Explicit model ids when the server does not list them

contextWindow.description: Fallback context window when the server does not report it

headers.markdownDescription: Extra request headers, e.g. `{ "X-Org": "${env:ORG_ID}" }`. Values may use `${env:NAME}` and `${secret:NAME}`.

timeoutMs.description: Least time to wait for the first token, in milliseconds (slow gateways, models that load on demand)

apiVersion.markdownDescription: Azure OpenAI `api-version` for deployment-style endpoints, e.g. `2024-10-21`. Not needed for the `/openai/v1` endpoint.

defaultModel.markdownDescription: Model used when only the provider id is given (`-m openrouter`, `localpilot.defaultModel: "openrouter"`).

modelsUrl.description: Where to read the model list when it is not <baseUrl>/models

extraBody.markdownDescription: Fields merged into every chat request, e.g. OpenRouter's `{ "provider": { "sort": "price" } }`.

modelOverrides.markdownDescription: Per-model settings by model id: `contextWindow`, `maxOutput`, `vision`, `reasoning`, `inputPrice` and `outputPrice` (US dollars per 1M tokens) and `temperature`.

localpilot.defaultModel.description: Default model as provider/model (e.g. ollama/gemma4:e4b). Empty = auto-pick the best tool-capable local model.

localpilot.contextWindow.description: Requested context window in tokens (num_ctx for Ollama), capped by the model's maximum. 0 = use the model's full native window (the largest it supports — needs enough RAM/VRAM). The same number drives compaction, so the conversation is summarised before the server would have to truncate it.

localpilot.temperature.markdownDescription: Sampling temperature for the agent. `-1` (the default) uses each model's own setting, as its makers tuned it — for example Gemma 4 and Qwen 3 ship 1.0, and at low temperatures they tend to repeat themselves until the token limit. Set 0–2 to force one value for every model. Inline completions, summaries and other short internal requests use their own low values.

enumDescriptions: Per task: high for Plan and Debug, medium for the agent and Multitask, low for Ask and subagents, none for quick helpers (auto-mode reviewer, inline edits, compaction summaries).
Never think: answers start immediately (sent explicitly; thinking models otherwise reason by default).
The model's default amount of thinking for every agent run.
Low effort for every agent run.
Medium effort for every agent run.
High effort for every agent run.
The most thinking the model offers (Claude's largest budget or max effort; high elsewhere).
localpilot.thinking.markdownDescription: Extended thinking for reasoning models (Ollama `think`, OpenAI-compatible `reasoning_effort`, OpenRouter `reasoning`, Claude's thinking budget or effort). Models that cannot think are never sent it. Quick helpers never think. Reasoning is shown as a collapsible step. A chat can choose its own level with the **Think** chip in the composer (`/thinking` in the CLI).

localpilot.keepAlive.description: How long Ollama keeps the model loaded after a request (e.g. 5m, 30m, -1 for forever). Avoids reload latency between turns.

localpilot.prewarm.description: Load the chat's model into memory as soon as you open the chat, focus the composer or switch models, so the first token is not preceded by a weight load. Ollama only; throttled per model unless the server reports it was unloaded.

localpilot.prompts.autoCorrect.description: Correct misspelled file names and code identifiers in your requests against the names in the workspace ("dicee.py" → "dice.py", "rollDise" → "rollDice") before the agent starts. Plain words are never changed; corrections are shown under your message.

localpilot.ollama.flashAttention.description: Start Ollama with flash attention (OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION). Faster prompt processing and a smaller KV cache on supported models. Applies when LocalPilot starts or restarts Ollama.

enumDescriptions: Full precision KV cache — most memory.
8-bit KV cache — about half the memory of f16, negligible quality loss (recommended).
4-bit KV cache — about a quarter of the memory; small quality loss on long contexts.
localpilot.ollama.kvCacheType.description: KV cache quantisation for Ollama (OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE). A smaller cache loads faster and lets large context windows stay on the GPU. Needs flash attention; applies when LocalPilot starts or restarts Ollama.

localpilot.memory.enabled.description: Let the agent read and save durable notes in .localpilot/memory (project) and global storage (user).

localpilot.memory.autoSave.markdownDescription: After a run with at least three tool calls in which the agent saved nothing itself, ask the same model whether the run revealed durable facts about the project — verified build and test commands, conventions, pitfalls and their fixes — and append them (at most three short notes) to project memory in `.localpilot/memory`. Runs after the answer, never delays it; anything that looks like a credential is dropped. Needs `#localpilot.memory.enabled#`.

localpilot.memory.maxNoteChars.markdownDescription: Largest size of one memory note. When a note grows past it, its oldest paragraphs are dropped (a leading heading is kept). Appending lines a note already has does nothing.

localpilot.memory.maxNotes.markdownDescription: Most memory notes kept per scope (project / global). Past it, the least recently updated notes are deleted (`README` is kept).

localpilot.sessions.retention.description: Maximum number of chats kept in this workspace's history. The oldest idle chats are removed automatically when a new one is created; pinned and running chats are never removed. 0 keeps everything.

localpilot.history.includeCli.markdownDescription: Show chats from the `localpilot` terminal CLI for the same folder in the chat history (marked **CLI**). They are read from `~/.localpilot/workspaces/` (or `LOCALPILOT_DATA_DIR`); continuing one here saves it with this workspace's chats. Takes effect after a window reload.

localpilot.compactionThreshold.description: Fraction of the context window at which older messages are pruned and summarised.

localpilot.showTips.markdownDescription: While the agent has been thinking for more than a few seconds, show short feature tips (steering, `@` mentions, `/compact`, checkpoints, …) in the chat's status row. Tips are built in; nothing is fetched.

enumDescriptions: The model writes a structured summary of the older messages. Falls back to basic when the summary fails or the transcript is too large for the model.
No model call: keeps every user message, the last few assistant replies verbatim and one line per earlier tool call. Instant and predictable.
Never compact automatically. Old tool outputs are still shortened; a conversation that outgrows the context window fails until you start a new chat or run /compact.
localpilot.compaction.strategy.markdownDescription: How the conversation is compacted when it fills the context window (at `#localpilot.compactionThreshold#`). Before any compaction the full transcript is archived beside the chat, so editing or restoring an earlier message brings the original messages back.

localpilot.maxToolOutputChars.description: Tool outputs longer than this are truncated (head + tail) before being sent to the model.

localpilot.maxConsecutiveMistakes.markdownDescription: Stop a run after this many steps in a row in which every tool call failed (or a tool call had to be repaired), and ask you for guidance. Any successful tool call resets the count; your next message continues normally. `0` = no limit.

localpilot.healing.enabled.markdownDescription: Self-healing engine: when a build, test, tool or model call fails, LocalPilot detects and classifies the failure, diagnoses it, fixes it and re-runs the relevant checks until the task is complete or a budget (attempts, time, approvals) is reached, then explains why and asks you. Off = today's behaviour (no quality gate, including the security check). Ignored in an untrusted workspace, so a cloned repository cannot turn it off.

localpilot.healing.autoDetect.markdownDescription: Classify tool, model and check failures after every step (category, severity, signature).

localpilot.healing.autoRetry.markdownDescription: Retry transient failures (model timeouts, unreachable servers, dropped MCP connections) with the category's backoff. Only calls that did not produce output are retried.

localpilot.healing.autoFix.markdownDescription: Inject diagnosis and fix steps for deterministic failures (compile errors, failing tests, lint). Off = detect and report only.

localpilot.healing.regressionRequired.markdownDescription: A task is only **completed** when the full relevant test suite passes after a fix, not just the affected tests.

localpilot.healing.maxRepairAttempts.markdownDescription: Most fix-and-recheck attempts per code-fix category (compile, TypeScript, build, tests, runtime). `0` = never fix automatically.

localpilot.healing.maxTotalAttempts.markdownDescription: Most recovery attempts per task across all categories. When it is reached the task stops with its root cause and the next action.

localpilot.healing.extraSteps.markdownDescription: Extra model steps the engine may grant for recovery beyond `#localpilot.maxIterations#`.

localpilot.healing.taskDeadlineMinutes.markdownDescription: Recovery deadline in minutes, counted from the first detected failure and applied only while a recovery is active. `0` = no deadline.

enumDescriptions: Run the project checks when the agent says it is done
Also run fast checks (typecheck, lint) after each batch of edits
localpilot.healing.checkTiming.markdownDescription: When the project checks (build, typecheck, lint, tests) run.

localpilot.healing.scopeTests.markdownDescription: Run the tests affected by the changed files first, before the full suite.

localpilot.healing.checkTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Default timeout per check in seconds (tests get twice as long). A check that times out is reported as unverified.

localpilot.healing.checkTimeBudgetSecond.markdownDescription: Total time in seconds one quality-gate run may spend on checks.

enumDescriptions: Record failures of the fast checks (typecheck + lint) before the first edit
Record failures of every check, including tests, before the first edit
No baseline: every failure counts as new
localpilot.healing.baseline.markdownDescription: Which checks run before the agent's first edit, so failures that already existed are not blamed on (or fixed in) the task.

id.description: Check id; an id of a discovered check (e.g. `npm:test`) overrides it. Ids starting with `security` are reserved for the built-in scan.

cwd.description: Workspace-relative folder (absolute paths and `..` are rejected).

scoped.description: Command for affected-only runs, with {files}, {tests} or {pkgs}.

required.description: A failing required check blocks completion.

when.description: Globs: only run when a changed file matches.

localpilot.healing.checks.markdownDescription: Project checks that override or add to the discovered ones (`package.json` scripts, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`…). Ignored in an untrusted workspace.

attempts.description: Recovery attempts for this category (clamped to its safety maximum).

localpilot.healing.policies.markdownDescription: Per-category retry policy overrides, e.g. `{ "unit_test": { "attempts": 2 } }`: `attempts`, `backoffMs` (array) and `timeoutSeconds`. Safety limits cannot be raised: `security` at most 3 remediation attempts, and `data_corruption`, `git_conflict`, `permission` and `loop` always escalate (0).

enumDescriptions: Ask before installing or adding a package
Never install: report the task as blocked
localpilot.healing.dependencyInstall.markdownDescription: Missing dependencies: installs always ask for approval, or never happen. User settings only.

enumDescriptions: Leave conflicted files untouched and ask you to review
localpilot.healing.gitConflicts.markdownDescription: Git merge conflicts are never resolved automatically: the conflicted files are left as they are and the task asks for your review.

enumDescriptions: Scan changed files offline for secrets and risky code
Also check dependencies for known vulnerabilities (asks for network access)
No security check
localpilot.healing.securityCheck.markdownDescription: Security check before a task completes. A finding blocks completion until it is fixed or you accept the risk; there is no automatic bypass. User settings only, so a repository cannot turn it off; a trusted workspace can still turn off the whole engine with `localpilot.healing.enabled`.

localpilot.healing.delegateFixes.markdownDescription: Fix independent groups of failures in parallel subagents.

enumDescriptions: Remember failures and fixes for this workspace (not shared)
Store them in the project's .localpilot folder
Do not remember failures
localpilot.healing.memory.markdownDescription: Failure memory: past failure signatures and the fixes that worked, offered as suggestions (always re-validated) when the same failure appears again.

enumDescriptions: GPT, Codex and gpt-oss models get apply_patch (the `*** Begin Patch` format they were trained on); other models get edit_file and write_file.
Always offer edit_file and write_file.
Always offer apply_patch instead of edit_file and write_file.
localpilot.editTool.markdownDescription: Which file-editing tool the agent gets. `apply_patch` changes, adds, moves and deletes several files in one call with a single approval.

enumDescriptions: Open a side-by-side diff of a proposed edit while its approval is pending; it closes when you approve or deny.
Also open the diff for edits that are approved automatically.
Never open a diff tab; edits happen in the background.
localpilot.diffPreview.markdownDescription: Side-by-side diff (`Original ↔ LocalPilot (proposed)`) of what `edit_file`, `write_file` and `apply_patch` are about to write.

localpilot.disabledTools.markdownDescription: Tools never offered to the model. Use LocalPilot names (`web_fetch`), Claude Code or Cline names (`Bash`, `WebSearch`, `execute_command`) or globs (`mcp_*`, `browser_*`). Also editable under **Settings → Agent & approvals → Tools**.

localpilot.pdf.maxReadSizeMB.markdownDescription: Largest PDF the agent may read with `read_pdf`, `read_file` or as an attachment.

localpilot.pdf.maxChars.markdownDescription: Most characters of PDF text returned per read (the tool output is still subject to `#localpilot.maxToolOutputChars#`).

enumDescriptions: Darken pages in dark themes, follow high-contrast themes exactly, original colours otherwise
Pages as printed
Inverted pages for dark rooms (photos look inverted too)
Warm paper tone
localpilot.pdfViewer.pageColors.markdownDescription: Page colours in the PDF viewer. `auto` darkens pages in dark themes and follows high-contrast themes exactly.

localpilot.pdfViewer.sidebar.markdownDescription: What the PDF viewer's sidebar shows when a file opens. `auto` shows the outline when the PDF has one, otherwise page thumbnails, and hides the sidebar when the view is narrower than 640 px.

localpilot.pdfViewer.defaultZoom.markdownDescription: Zoom for PDFs opened for the first time. Files you have read before reopen at their last page and zoom.

localpilot.pdfViewer.rangeThresholdMB.markdownDescription: PDFs larger than this load on demand, page by page, instead of all at once.

localpilot.pdfViewer.maxFileSizeMB.markdownDescription: Ask before opening PDFs larger than this.

localpilot.markdownViewer.scrollSync.markdownDescription: Keep the Markdown reader and the source editor scrolled to the same place. Double-click a block in the reader to jump to its line in the source.

localpilot.markdownViewer.outlineDepth.markdownDescription: Deepest heading level shown in the Markdown reader's outline and in an inline `[[toc]]`.

enumDescriptions: A collapsed Properties table above the document
The Properties table, open
Do not show front matter
localpilot.markdownViewer.frontMatter.markdownDescription: How YAML front matter is shown above a document in the Markdown reader.

localpilot.markdownViewer.mermaid.markdownDescription: Render ```` ```mermaid ```` code blocks as diagrams in the Markdown reader. Mermaid is bundled and works offline.

enumDescriptions: Light colours, whatever the editor theme
The colours of the current VS Code theme
localpilot.markdownViewer.exportTheme.markdownDescription: Colours used by **Export as HTML / PDF** in the Markdown reader.

enumDescriptions: Run every command without asking (destructive ones still ask, see `#localpilot.approvals.dangerousAlwaysAsk#`).

Run read-only commands (`ls`, `git status`, `grep`…) and routine test, lint and build commands (`npm test`, `tsc`, `pytest`, `cargo test`, `go vet`, `make test`) without asking; ask for everything else.
Ask before every command.
Never run commands.
localpilot.approvals.terminal.markdownDescription: Approval policy for running shell commands. The model can mark a command `requires_approval`; such a command asks even under `always` or `safe`.

localpilot.approvals.dangerousAlwaysAsk.markdownDescription: Ask before a destructive-looking command (`rm -rf /…`, `sudo`, `git push --force`, `git reset --hard`, `mkfs`…) even when `#localpilot.approvals.terminal#` is `always`. Such a prompt is never answered by **Allow for session** or auto mode.

localpilot.approvals.network.description: Approval policy for web search / fetch and the browser tools.

localpilot.approvals.mcp.markdownDescription: Approval policy for tools from MCP servers. A server's `autoApprove` list runs those tools without asking even when this is `ask`; `never` blocks every MCP tool.

localpilot.autoMode.enabled.markdownDescription: **Auto mode**: an action that would ask for approval (see `#localpilot.approvals.terminal#` and the other approval settings, or an `ask` permission rule) is first reviewed by a small local model. The reviewer approves actions that clearly serve your request and stay inside the project. Everything else still asks you. Pushes, `sudo`, recursive deletes, piping downloads into a shell, publishing and writes to secrets or `.git` always ask. The reviewer can only approve, never deny, and any reviewer error falls back to asking. Turn it on or off with **LocalPilot: Turn Auto Mode On/Off**.

localpilot.autoMode.model.markdownDescription: Model that reviews actions in auto mode (`provider/model`). Empty = the fastest suitable installed model.

enumDescriptions: Notify only while the chat view is hidden or the VS Code window is not focused.
Always notify.
Never notify.
localpilot.notifications.markdownDescription: Native notifications: a chat run finished, or an auto-approved command is still running after 30 seconds (also shown in the status bar). The terminal CLI rings the terminal bell when a run longer than 10 seconds finishes, unless this is `off`.

localpilot.parallel.maxConcurrency.description: Max concurrent tool calls / subagents. When LocalPilot starts Ollama it also requests this many parallel slots (OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL, capped at 4) so subagents really run concurrently.

localpilot.parallel.maxSubagentDepth.description: Levels of subagents allowed. 1 = only the main agent may delegate (its subagents cannot start their own); 2 = subagents may delegate one level deeper; up to 4.

localpilot.queue.concurrency.markdownDescription: How many tasks from the **task queue** (Agents view → Queue, or **LocalPilot: Queue Agent Task…**) run at once. `1` runs them one after another; higher values run them side by side, each in its own isolated worktree when `#localpilot.worktrees.mode#` is `parallel` or `always`. Tasks can also wait for other tasks to succeed first. The queue is saved per workspace and resumes after a reload.

enumDescriptions: Every agent chat works in its own isolated copy of the repository (a git worktree); you review and apply its changes.
Only agents started together (Run Tasks in Parallel, Best of N) are isolated; a single chat edits the workspace directly.
Agents always edit the workspace directly.
localpilot.worktrees.mode.markdownDescription: Isolate agents in **git worktrees** so several can edit the same files at once without clobbering each other or your open editors. A worktree starts as a copy of your checkout *including uncommitted work*; when the agent is done you **Apply to workspace** (changes land as ordinary uncommitted edits, 3-way merged on conflict) or **Discard**. Setup commands for new worktrees (e.g. `npm install`) go in `.localpilot/worktrees.json`: `{ "setup": ["npm ci"] }`. Needs a git repository; otherwise agents edit directly.

localpilot.worktrees.location.markdownDescription: Folder that holds the worktrees (one sub-folder per repository). Empty = `~/.localpilot/worktrees`.

localpilot.telemetry.enabled.markdownDescription: Record local usage metrics — model calls, tokens and latency, tool runs, agent turns, inline completions, provider health — to daily JSONL files in `~/.localpilot/telemetry` for the **LocalPilot: Open Dashboard** page. Everything stays on this machine — unless you turn on `#localpilot.storage.redis.enabled#`, which sends it to the Redis server you configure; nothing is ever sent to a third party.

localpilot.telemetry.retentionDays.markdownDescription: Days of metrics and log files to keep on disk; older files are deleted automatically. `0` keeps everything.

localpilot.telemetry.otlp.enabled.markdownDescription: Also send telemetry to **your own OpenTelemetry collector** (otel-collector, Grafana Alloy, Langfuse, Phoenix…) over OTLP/HTTP JSON: events and log lines as logs, usage as metrics, and with `traces` in `#localpilot.telemetry.otlp.exporters#` run/model/tool spans. The standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` (only `http/json`) and `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL` variables override these settings. Run **LocalPilot: Test OTLP Connection** to check the endpoint.

localpilot.telemetry.otlp.endpoint.markdownDescription: Base URL of the OTLP/HTTP receiver; `/v1/logs`, `/v1/metrics` and `/v1/traces` are appended.

localpilot.telemetry.otlp.headers.markdownDescription: Extra HTTP headers for every export, e.g. `{ "Authorization": "Basic …" }` for Langfuse. `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` (`k=v,k2=v2`) adds to and overrides these.

localpilot.telemetry.otlp.metricsInterva.markdownDescription: Seconds between metric exports (cumulative counters and histograms).

localpilot.telemetry.otlp.exporters.markdownDescription: What to export: `otlp` sends logs and metrics to the endpoint, `traces` sends run, model-call and tool-call spans (`gen_ai.*` attributes) to `/v1/traces`, and `console` also prints every export to the LocalPilot log.

localpilot.telemetry.otlp.traceSamplePer.markdownDescription: Share of agent runs traced when `traces` is exported (a run's model and tool spans are kept or dropped together).

localpilot.telemetry.otlp.recordContent.markdownDescription: Put prompts, replies, tool arguments and tool results on trace spans. Off by default: spans then carry only names, timings, token counts and outcomes.

localpilot.storage.sessionsInMemory.markdownDescription: Chat transcripts kept in memory. Every chat stays in the history list, but only the most recently used transcripts (plus running chats and the one on screen) are held in RAM; the others are read back from disk when you open or search them. Lower it to save memory with long histories.

localpilot.storage.redis.enabled.markdownDescription: Optional: store telemetry events and the log in **Redis** (capped streams) instead of daily files, and — with **Redis Stack** (RedisTimeSeries) — as labelled time series you can chart in Grafana or RedisInsight. The extension then keeps only a short log tail in memory and the dashboard reads history in batches. Falls back to files whenever Redis is unreachable. Telemetry (model and tool names, timings, log lines — never prompts or file contents) then goes to the server in `#localpilot.storage.redis.url#`, so keep that on this machine unless you trust the server. Run **LocalPilot: Set Up Redis Storage** to install or connect one.

localpilot.storage.redis.url.markdownDescription: Redis connection for `#localpilot.storage.redis.enabled#`: `redis://[user:password@]host:port[/db]`, or `rediss://` for TLS. Keep it on `127.0.0.1` unless the server is protected — telemetry includes model names, tool names and log lines.

localpilot.supervisor.enabled.markdownDescription: Keep local support services running while VS Code is open. **Ollama** (local only) is started when it has models downloaded, serves `#localpilot.defaultModel#` or has run this session, and restarted if it stops. A run that needs a stopped local Ollama also starts it, whatever this setting. **Redis** is restarted when `#localpilot.storage.redis.enabled#` is on, using its Docker container or a native `redis-server`. After 4 failed restarts in a row LocalPilot stops trying and tells you. See **LocalPilot: Show Background Services**.

localpilot.supervisor.intervalSeconds.markdownDescription: How often the background services are checked.

localpilot.supervisor.autoInstall.markdownDescription: When no local model server is found at startup, install **Ollama** and a starter model that fits this machine without asking first (a cancellable progress notification shows the download — usually several GB). Off: LocalPilot offers the one-click setup instead.

localpilot.autoClarify.markdownDescription: When a request is short, vague or refers to "this"/"it" without naming a target, give the agent a snapshot of the active editor, open files, recent edits, errors and git changes so it can state its interpretation (`Understood as: …`) and proceed, asking only when two readings would lead to materially different work.

enumDescriptions: New features and open-ended or large requests: ask up to 4 questions (explained options, a recommended pick) in one card, state a short plan, then start. Clear requests start right away.
Every change: ask first, then show the plan and wait for your OK before editing.
Only when two readings would lead to materially different work.
localpilot.clarify.questions.markdownDescription: When the agent asks you questions before it starts. Questions appear as a card in the chat: each option explains what choosing it means, one is marked recommended, some allow several picks, and you can always answer in your own words or **Skip** (the agent then goes with its recommendations).

localpilot.webSearch.enabled.markdownDescription: Let the agent use the internet: `web_search`, `web_fetch` and the browser tools are offered and `@https://…` mentions are fetched. Off: those tools are removed from every request and URL mentions are refused. Model providers are not affected.

localpilot.preferredLanguage.markdownDescription: Language the agent answers in, in the chat and the CLI. `auto` adds no instruction (the model usually follows your language). Code, identifiers and commands stay as they are.

localpilot.webSearch.provider.description: duckduckgo needs no key; searxng is self-hosted; brave/tavily need an API key.

localpilot.inlineCompletion.enabled.description: Ghost-text completions from a local FIM model (qwen2.5-coder, codestral, starcoder2…).

localpilot.inlineCompletion.model.description: provider/model for completions. Empty = the smallest FIM-capable model that fits this machine.

localpilot.mcpServers.markdownDescription: MCP servers whose tools are exposed to the agent. A local server is started from a command: `{ "filesystem": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "."] } }`. A remote server is reached at a URL over Streamable HTTP (or HTTP+SSE for a URL ending in `/sse` or `"type": "sse"`), with optional headers: `{ "github": { "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:GITHUB_TOKEN}" } } }`. Every field accepts `${env:NAME}` and `${secret:NAME}`. Servers are also read from `<workspace>/.mcp.json` (started once you trust them) and `~/.localpilot/mcp.json`; this setting wins on a name clash.

url.markdownDescription: Remote server endpoint (`https://…`). Use instead of `command`.

enumDescriptions: Local process (command)
Streamable HTTP (current MCP remote transport)
HTTP + Server-Sent Events (older remote servers)

headers.markdownDescription: Request headers for a remote server, e.g. `{ "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:TOKEN}" }`.

timeout.markdownDescription: Seconds a request to this server (a tool call, a listing) may take before it fails. Default 60.

autoApprove.markdownDescription: Tools of this server (as the server names them) that run without asking.

oauthClient.markdownDescription: A client you registered with this remote server's OAuth authorization server (redirect URIs `http://127.0.0.1:1456/mcp/oauth/callback` … port 1461). Without it LocalPilot registers itself when the server asks you to sign in. `clientSecret` accepts `${secret:NAME}`.

localpilot.mcp.watchServerFiles.markdownDescription: Restart a local (stdio) MCP server 500 ms after its script changes: a workspace `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs` or `.py` file named in its command or arguments, or a file under `build/` or `dist/`. Handy while you develop a server.

localpilot.repos.markdownDescription: Extra repositories the agent can work across, name → folder, e.g. `{ "api": "~/src/api", "web": "~/src/web" }`. The folders of a multi-root workspace and a workspace's `.localpilot/repos.json` are included automatically. The agent lists, searches and runs commands in them with the `repos` tool and runs one subagent per repository for cross-repository changes.

localpilot.pluginPaths.markdownDescription: Extra folders containing Claude Code-style plugins (a folder with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` bundling `commands/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, `hooks/hooks.json` and `.mcp.json`). `.localpilot/plugins`, `.claude/plugins`, `~/.localpilot/plugins` and `~/.claude/plugins` are scanned automatically; disable one with `enabledPlugins` in `settings.json`.

localpilot.plugins.marketplaces.markdownDescription: Plugin marketplaces to search and install from (**LocalPilot: Browse Plugins…**, `localpilot plugin search`): `owner/repo` on GitHub, any git URL, or a local folder — each with a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` in Claude Code's format. Marketplaces are fetched with `git`, so private repositories work with your git credentials.

localpilot.checkpoints.enabled.markdownDescription: Take a checkpoint before each message you send: in a git repository a private ref (`refs/localpilot/checkpoints/<chat>/<turn>`) records the working tree, including untracked files and changes made by shell commands, without touching your index, branches or `git stash list`. Outside git (or with this off) only the files the agent edits are snapshotted. Checkpoints are deleted with the chat.

localpilot.hooks.enabled.markdownDescription: Run the hooks configured in `.localpilot/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.json` (and `~/.claude/settings.json`): shell commands on `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `SessionStart`, `PreCompact` and `Notification`, with the Claude Code stdin/exit-code protocol (exit 2 blocks). Turn off to ignore hooks from a repository you do not trust.

localpilot.skillsPaths.description: Extra folders containing skills (each skill is a folder with SKILL.md). `.localpilot/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.github/skills`, `~/.agents/skills` are scanned automatically.

localpilot.skills.builtin.markdownDescription: Load the skills bundled with LocalPilot (requirements, design, implement, test, debug, review, deploy, …). A workspace or user skill with the same name overrides the bundled one; copy a bundled skill from the extension's `skills/` folder into `.localpilot/skills/` to customise it.

localpilot.skills.repositories.markdownDescription: Skill catalog: GitHub repositories or folders (`owner/repo[/path][@ref]`, github.com URLs) in the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format whose skills LocalPilot can install when a request matches one that is not installed yet. The first repository wins when several offer the same name. Browse them with **LocalPilot: Browse Skill Registry (Quick Pick)…**. The index is cached in `~/.localpilot/skill-catalog.json` and refreshed daily; set `GITHUB_TOKEN` for private repositories or higher API limits.

enumDescriptions: Install the best-matching catalog skill as the request starts, then load it — no prompt.
Show an "Install …" chip under the request; nothing is downloaded until you click it.
Never look up the catalog for a request (Browse Skill Registry (Quick Pick)… still works).
localpilot.skills.autoInstall.markdownDescription: When a request matches a skill from `#localpilot.skills.repositories#` better than any installed skill (planning, design docs, debugging, writing Markdown, PDFs, …), install it on the spot or offer it. A skill you removed after an automatic install, or declined, is not installed again.

enumDescriptions: ~/.localpilot/skills — available in every workspace, nothing added to the project.
.localpilot/skills in the workspace — shared with everyone who opens the project.
localpilot.skills.autoInstallScope.description: Where automatically installed skills are stored.

localpilot.skills.disabled.markdownDescription: Skill names the agent must not see or load (not in the prompt, not suggested, `load_skill` refuses them) while they stay on disk. Toggle skills in **Settings → Skills** instead of editing this by hand.

localpilot.systemPromptAppend.description: Extra instructions appended to the system prompt (coding conventions, preferences…).

localpilot.showWelcomeOnStartup.markdownDescription: Open the **Setup** screen the first time LocalPilot starts without a reachable model server or default model. Run it again any time with *LocalPilot: Open Setup*.

enumDescriptions: Primary Side Bar (left, with the Explorer), under the LocalPilot activity bar icon.
Secondary Side Bar (right), where Copilot Chat lives.
Bottom panel, next to the Terminal and Problems.
An editor tab in the main area, like a file.
localpilot.chat.location.markdownDescription: Where the chat opens. Changing it moves the Chat view there with VS Code's own view mechanics, so drag-and-drop, *Move View* and *Reset Location* keep working; the Agents view and the LocalPilot activity bar icon stay in the Primary Side Bar. Also available as *LocalPilot: Move Chat To…* in the chat toolbar and the status bar menu. The LocalPilot icon in the editor title bar and the status bar always opens the chat wherever it is.

localpilot.models.autoSetup.markdownDescription: When no local model is found, offer to set one up automatically: start or install Ollama and download the smallest coder model that suits this machine (plus a tiny completion model when it fits).

enumDescriptions: Learn from usage and apply the best installed model per role automatically (with Undo). A model you picked by hand is only replaced when it is measurably failing.
Learn from usage for Auto routing and offer better picks in a notification; never write settings without asking.
Do not learn from usage.
localpilot.models.autoTune.markdownDescription: Learn from local telemetry which of your **installed** models work best on this machine for each role (chat & agent, Plan mode, coding and read-only subagents, inline completions, images): how often their runs finish, generation speed, time to first token, errors and completion acceptance. Auto routing prefers the models that perform; `auto` also writes better picks to `#localpilot.defaultModel#`, `#localpilot.routing.reasoning#`, `#localpilot.routing.coding#` and the other role settings. Needs `#localpilot.telemetry.enabled#`; nothing leaves the machine. Run *LocalPilot: Tune Models From Usage* to review now.

localpilot.colibri.path.markdownDescription: Folder of a [colibri](https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri) checkout (the one with `c/coli`). colibri runs very large mixture-of-experts models (GLM-5.2, DeepSeek V4 Flash, Qwen3-Coder-30B…) by keeping the dense part in RAM and streaming experts from disk. *LocalPilot: Start colibri* runs `coli serve` from here; empty = `coli` on PATH. A running `coli serve` is detected either way.

localpilot.colibri.model.markdownDescription: Model for *LocalPilot: Start colibri*: a colibri catalog id (`qwen3-coder-30b`, `qwen36-35b`, `glm-5.2`, `deepseek-v4-flash`…) or a folder with a model already on disk. Empty: colibri's setup recommends one for this machine. *Start colibri → Switch model…* picks another.

localpilot.colibri.port.markdownDescription: Port `coli serve` listens on. Auto-detect also probes it when it is not 8000.

localpilot.colibri.kvSlots.markdownDescription: `--kv-slots` for *LocalPilot: Start colibri*: conversations colibri decodes together, each with its own cached prefix, so parallel agents do not evict each other's context. Each slot costs a few hundred MB; capped by `#localpilot.parallel.maxConcurrency#`.

localpilot.gateways.litellmConfig.markdownDescription: LiteLLM proxy config file (`model_list`) for *LocalPilot: Start Gateway*. Asked for on first start.

localpilot.colibri.modelsDir.markdownDescription: Where colibri downloads models (`coli setup --dir`). Empty: `~/colibri-models`. Pick a disk with room: models are 19 GB to 1.6 TB.

enumDescriptions: CUDA, then Vulkan, then the CPU, whichever this machine supports (Apple Silicon uses Metal automatically)
CPU only
Vulkan GPUs (Linux, Windows)
NVIDIA GPUs with the CUDA toolkit (Linux)
localpilot.colibri.backend.markdownDescription: Engine colibri builds or downloads at setup (`coli setup --backend`).

localpilot.models.disabled.markdownDescription: `provider/model` ids hidden from the model picker, routing and the status bar. Toggle models in **Settings → Models** instead of editing this by hand.

localpilot.routing.enabled.markdownDescription: Pick the right model per task automatically: a vision model for turns with images, the smallest fill-in-the-middle model for inline completions, the configured reasoning model in Plan mode, and the best available model when the default is offline or disabled.

localpilot.routing.vision.description: provider/model used for turns that include images when the session model cannot see. Empty = best available vision model.

localpilot.browser.chromePath.markdownDescription: Path to a Chromium-based browser used for headless web-page screenshots (`browser_screenshot` tool, *Screenshot a Web Page…*). Empty = auto-detect Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave or Arc.

localpilot.routing.reasoning.description: provider/model used in Plan mode (e.g. ollama/gemma4:12b or ollama/gpt-oss:20b). Empty = keep the session model.

localpilot.routing.fast.markdownDescription: provider/model for read-only subagents (`explore`, `clarifier`, `researcher`), which run many short tool calls in parallel. Empty = the smallest tool-capable model that fits this machine; `session` = always use the session model.

localpilot.routing.coding.markdownDescription: provider/model for implementing subagents (`coder`, `tester`, `debugger`, `docs`). Empty = keep the session model.

localpilot.routing.parallelModels.markdownDescription: Run parallel work on several models at once. When workers (or Auto chats) all land on a model that is already serving as many requests as it can — one, on a server that answers one request per model at a time — the extra ones go to a comparable idle model that fits in memory alongside (same capabilities, similar quality score), instead of queuing. A model you picked explicitly for a chat is never swapped; each worker's lane shows the model that answered it.

localpilot.terminal.runInIntegratedTermi.markdownDescription: Run the agent's `run_command` calls in a visible **LocalPilot Agent** terminal (via shell integration) so you can watch them live. Falls back to a hidden process when the shell has no integration or when disabled.

localpilot.terminal.reveal.description: Show the LocalPilot Agent terminal (without stealing focus) when the agent runs a command.

localpilot.terminal.autoDetachSeconds.markdownDescription: Seconds a `run_command` call may run before the agent proceeds while it keeps running (its later output goes to a log the agent can read). `0` = never detach: the command is stopped at its timeout instead.

localpilot.terminal.shellIntegrationTime.markdownDescription: How long (ms) to wait for shell integration in the **LocalPilot Agent** terminal before running the command in a hidden process instead. Raise it when a slow shell startup (large `.zshrc`, conda) makes the agent fall back.

localpilot.terminal.profile.markdownDescription: Shell the agent's commands run in: `default` (VS Code's default shell) or the name of a profile from `terminal.integrated.profiles` for this OS. Used by the LocalPilot Agent terminal, background commands and the hidden fallback process. Pick one with **LocalPilot: Select Agent Terminal Profile…**.

localpilot.edit.reportNewErrors.markdownDescription: After the agent edits or writes a file, wait up to 1.5 s for the language server and append the **new** errors in that file (at most 10) to the tool result, so the agent fixes what it broke. No effect in the CLI, which has no language servers.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with LocalPilot
walkthroughs.description: Connect a local model server, pick a model and run your first agent task — all on your machine.

steps.title: Connect a model server
steps.description:
LocalPilot works with Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The setup screen finds running servers and recommends a model — or installs Ollama and a model sized for this machine in one click.
[Open setup](command:localpilot.openWelcome)
[Manage models](command:localpilot.manageModels)

steps.title: Open the chat
steps.description:
Ask questions, or switch to **Agent** mode to let LocalPilot plan, edit files and run commands with your approval.
[Open chat](command:localpilot.openChat)

steps.title: Decide how autonomous the agent is
steps.description:
Choose **Careful**, **Balanced** or **Autonomous**, or set each approval individually. Every file edit is tracked and can be undone.
[Agent & approvals](command:localpilot.openSettings?%22agent%22)

steps.title: Run agents in parallel
steps.description:
Give several tasks at once — each runs as its own agent while you keep working.
[Run tasks in parallel](command:localpilot.runParallelTasks)

steps.title: Work in the editor
steps.description:
Edit a selection in place with Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+K, fix problems from the light bulb, and explain or fix terminal output.
[Try inline edit](command:localpilot.inlineEdit)

steps.title: Extend with skills and MCP
steps.description:
Teach the agent your workflows with skills, connect tools through MCP servers, or install a plugin that bundles both.
[Manage skills](command:localpilot.manageSkills)
[Browse plugins](command:localpilot.browsePlugins)

steps.title: Turn on inline completions
steps.description:
Ghost-text from a small local FIM model such as `qwen2.5-coder:1.5b-base`.
[Inline completions](command:localpilot.openSettings?%22completions%22)

scripts.compile: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production && node scripts/check-assets.js
scripts.pretest: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile && npm run lint
